comments.text:
I've watched EVERY video on this subject and I need to clear up one thing.  They drove up the mountain road at night and only stopped the car once they had reached the snow line and decided to stop and walk.  A snow-cat (like the one in "The Shining") had earlier in the week rolled and plowed a wide path from the main road a little further up the mountain past where they stopped their car.  Then it went down where there are a maze of small dirt roads throughout the woods in the middle of the wilderness between the car and the trailers.  But the snow-cat had made one long track, with many twists and turns, right up to the trailers and had turned around and went back the same way.  

When the boys walked up there, they followed the plowed path through the mountains that led directly to the trailers, because that's where the path went.  They may have been thinking they'd find a house with a phone they could use.  By the time a search was under way, several blizzards had covered all these tracks and made the roads all impassible.  Once they got to the trailer, or died trying, they were essentially stranded until the spring, at which time I think Gary Mathias hiked up to the main road and either hitched it or hiked it out of the mountains and took off to disappear into wherever he decided to live afterwards.  

Regarding the storehouse of food, I fear you are right.  They probably were afraid of getting in trouble for breaking the lock and "stealing" food.  They were not thinking very rationally because of their conditions, but knew to follow "rules".  The propane system is also not nearly as easy to operate as people think.  If they had trouble using a phone, figuring out that propane would have been like advanced molecular physics to them.

comments.text: Whenever I think of this story, I'm reminded of a night when I took a wrong turn coming back from a weekend at a remote campground. It came and went, and I thought I must be closer to the main road than I thought. I drove practically in circles trying to get to what I thought was the main road. It wasn't until I stopped the car and got out that I realized the lights I was seeing through the trees weren't from the highway. The light was from a train on a railroad, probably miles away. Train headlight beams make wide sweeping circles, which is why it looked intermittent through the trees. What I thought was cars passing was just the skipping of the headlight beam circling.  Did the boys think they saw a light or something that would lead them to civilization and help only to have it be a distant train or lights from a far off highway or something that was much further away than they could have known? The situation is so heartbreaking.
